D04.obligation: Carry out periodic updation of KYC for low-risk customers
D04.quote: carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers

D04.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
D04.obligation: Ensure the updation of KYC for low-risk individual customers within one year of it falling due
D04.quote: in respect of an individual customer who is categorised as low-risk, the NBFC shall allow all transactions and ensure the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC

D04.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | E. On-going Due Diligence > Updation / Periodic Updation of KYC | para 42
D04.obligation: Ensure the updation of KYC for low-risk individual customers up to the specified date if later than one year after falling due
D04.quote: in respect of an individual customer who is categorised as low-risk, the NBFC shall allow all transactions and ensure the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC or up to June 30, 2026, whichever is later

D05.source: Know Your Customer Directions, 2025 | Secrecy Obligations and Sharing of Information: > Registry (CKYCR) | para 63
D05.obligation: Capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR
D05.quote: the NBFC shall capture customer’s KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.
D05.trigger: commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer

D06.source: Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026 | Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India > B. Modalities of Reporting Incidents of Fraud | paras 43-45
D06.obligation: Furnish FMR in individual fraud cases to RBI
D06.quote: The Applicable NBFC shall furnish FMR in individual fraud cases, irrespective of the amount involved, immediately but not later than 14 days from the date of classification of an incident / account as fraud.
D06.trigger: date of classification of an incident / account as fraud

D07.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter II - Definitions and General Requirements > C. Early identification and reporting of stress | paras 18-21
D07.obligation: Report credit information, including classification of an account as SMA, to the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC) on a monthly basis.
D07.quote: A NBFC shall report credit information, including classification of an account as SMA, to Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC), on all borrowers having aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above with them, on a monthly basis.
D07.applies_to: all borrowers having aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above

D07.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter II - Definitions and General Requirements > C. Early identification and reporting of stress | paras 18-21
D07.obligation: Submit a weekly report of instances of default by eligible borrowers by close of business on every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday.
D07.quote: A NBFC shall submit a weekly report of instances of default by all borrowers (with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above) by close of business on every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday happens to be a holiday.
D07.applies_to: all borrowers (with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above)

D08.source: Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025 | Chapter III - Additional Prudential Norms applicable to an NBFC classified as NBFC – Base Layer (NBFC – BL) > A. Asset Classification | paras 43-45
D08.obligation: Adopt the NPA classification norm of more than 150 days overdue as part of the glide path.
D08.applies_to: applicable NBFCs (excluding NBFCs already required to follow the 90-day NPA norm)

D08.source: Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025 | Chapter III - Additional Prudential Norms applicable to an NBFC classified as NBFC – Base Layer (NBFC – BL) > A. Asset Classification | paras 43-45
D08.obligation: Adopt the NPA classification norm of more than 120 days overdue as part of the glide path.
D08.applies_to: applicable NBFCs (excluding NBFCs already required to follow the 90-day NPA norm)

D08.source: Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025 | Chapter III - Additional Prudential Norms applicable to an NBFC classified as NBFC – Base Layer (NBFC – BL) > A. Asset Classification | paras 43-45
D08.obligation: Adopt the NPA classification norm of more than 90 days overdue as part of the glide path.
D08.applies_to: applicable NBFCs (excluding NBFCs already required to follow the 90-day NPA norm)

D10.source: Compliance Function Directions, 2026 | Chapter IV - Chief Compliance Officer > B. Authority, Stature, and Independence | paras 21-25
D10.obligation: The Board / ACB must meet the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) at quarterly intervals on a one-to-one basis without the presence of senior management, including the MD & CEO.
D10.quote: In case the CCO reports to the MD & CEO, the Board / ACB shall meet the CCO at quarterly intervals on a one-to-one basis, without the presence of the senior management, including MD & CEO.
D10.applies_to: NBFCs where the CCO reports to the MD & CEO

D11.source: Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 | Chapter VI - Special Cases of Restructuring > C. Reporting Requirements | para 122
D11.obligation: Upload the data on relief measures on the CIMS portal within 30 days from the end of the half-year
D11.quote: NBFC shall upload the data on relief measures on a half-yearly basis within 30 days from the end of the half-year (September 30thand March 31stof every year) on the CIMS portal.
